title: Where Can Wisdom Be Found?
overview: This poem praises how deep human skill can dig for treasure, then asks where wisdom can be found, and answers that only God truly knows.

parts.label: Miners dig deep (vv. 1-6)
parts.note: Ancient miners pushed into total darkness, hung on ropes in remote shafts, and broke open rock to reach silver, gold, iron, copper and gems. The point is how far human cleverness and effort can reach into hidden places.

parts.label: A path no animal knows (vv. 7-11)
parts.note: Not even a falcon's sharp eye or a prowling lion has been where miners go, as they split hard rock and reach the sources of underground streams. People really can bring hidden things into the light.

parts.label: Wisdom cannot be dug up or bought (vv. 12-19)
parts.note: Yet no one can mine wisdom, here meaning a true grasp of how and why God runs the world, and even the deep sea says it is not there. Ophir and Cush were famous faraway sources of gold and gems, and even their finest treasures cannot buy it.

parts.label: Hidden even from Death (vv. 20-22)
parts.note: Wisdom is hidden from every living creature, even the sharp-eyed birds of the sky. Destruction and Death, pictured as speakers for the world of the dead, admit they have only heard a rumor of it.

parts.label: Only God knows the way (vv. 23-27)
parts.note: God sees everything, and when he set the force of the wind, measured the waters and gave the rain and thunder their paths, he looked at wisdom, weighed it and set it in place. Christians later read this pictured wisdom in light of Jesus, whom the New Testament calls the Word through whom all things were made.

parts.label: Wisdom for human beings (v. 28)
parts.note: People cannot see God's whole plan, but their share of wisdom is to hold God in deep reverence (the old word is "fear") and to turn away from evil. This echoes how chapter 1 describes Job himself, and many read it as a quiet rebuke to friends who claimed to know exactly why he was suffering.

disagreement: Readers differ on whether this poem is Job's own voice or a pause in the story added by the book's author, which changes whether it shows Job finding peace with not knowing or the author commenting on the whole debate.
think: Is there a kind of understanding that no amount of skill, effort or money can get you, and if so, how would you go looking for it?
